## Conclusions
- **Baseline reproduces.** Local CLIP ViT-B/16 gets 87.35 vs 86.97 measured on the S22 by the teammate's notebook
  (TFLite). The gap is plausibly runtime numerics; experiment 003+ checks QNN fidelity directly.
- **The official sample skips input normalization.** It exports `clip.visual` and feeds [0,1] pixels. Adding CLIP's
  mean/std inside the graph (`clip-b16-norm`) gives +1.5 points. We report a "fixed baseline" next to the official one,
  so that part of our gain isn't credited to compression.
- **The sample can't rank models.** With 56 queries the 95% CI is about ±6 points, and no paired difference vs. the
  baseline excludes 0.
- **Decision:** build a larger LPCVC-style validation set (→ experiment 002) and keep the sample as a held-out check
  only. Never use it to select.
